game: CIN@BAL Week 7 2026, BAL +3, total 46.5, kickoff/venue not in pack, weather not saved

script.base: Cincinnati is a 3-point road favorite (implied CIN 24.8 / BAL 21.8 on 46.5), so the book expects a one-score game, not a shootout and not a blowout. Lamar Jackson is out, so Baltimore's base plan is Derrick Henry (64 carries, 233 yards in weeks 4-6) plus Tyler Huntley, while Cincinnati still has to throw to reach 24.8 into a Ravens defense that blitzes 31%.
script.flip1: Baltimore leans on Henry, takes an early lead, and Cincinnati abandons Chase Brown (35 carries / 110 yards in weeks 3-5). Higgins and Chase targets rise in a chase script; Brown's rush line dies, and Henry's late carries go up if the lead holds.
script.flip2: The 31% blitz shows up (Burrow EPA/dropback -0.11 vs blitz, +0.24 vs none), Cincinnati falls behind, and Baltimore never has to throw. Henry's carries stay high only if the game stays close; if Baltimore trails by two scores, Henry is scripted out and Huntley is forced to Flowers and Andrews.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game report: Lamar Jackson Out (ankle). No pass chart for the replacement; Huntley is the only other BAL QB with rush volume in the pack (12 carries / 68 yards in the weeks 4-6 rush split; last listed rush games 18, 22, 28). Jackson's own L3 rush was already tiny (2/20), so the carry vacuum goes to Henry first and Huntley second, not to a same-position QB prop. Jaylinn Hawkins Out (knee, S) and T.J. Tampa Doubtful (knee, CB) thin the deep/outside shell and help CIN air-yard targets, led by Tee Higgins (27 targets, 269 yards, 363 air in weeks 3-5) over Ja'Marr Chase (25/202/235). Tavius Robinson Out (pectoral, LB) helps CIN TE/RB/slot: Mike Gesicki 10 targets / 81 yards, Chase Brown 17/100, D. Meyers 16/123. Broderick Washington is only Questionable (ankle, DE), so do not bank on a pass-rush absence. No CIN offensive injuries are in the report. Inactives (~90 min pre-kick) are not in the pack.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting saved, so MOFO/MOFC and man/zone are unknown. Location YPA is the proxy. BAL defense: left 6.36 (74 att), middle 8.3 (44), right 6.56 (79) — middle is the soft spot. CIN defense: left 7.57 (53), middle 10.08 (38), right 6.04 (73) — middle is a clear bleed.
matchup.pressure: BAL blitz rate 31% and Burrow is worse when blitzed (EPA/db -0.11 vs blitz, +0.24 vs none), which hits deep WR yards and should funnel quick throws to RB/TE. CIN blitzes only 16%; BAL EPA/db is +0.37 vs blitz and +0.15 vs none, but that sample is mostly with Jackson, who is out.
matchup.bleeds: CIN run defense allows 5.30 YPC and 21 runs of 10+ over 5 games — the structural bleed. BAL run defense is sound at 3.85 YPC and only 13 runs of 10+. Explosive passes: BAL 17 of 20+ for 212 yards, CIN 17 for 181.
matchup.overlap: Henry's workhorse share (64 of 83 BAL rushes in weeks 4-6) runs into the 5.30 YPC front. Higgins' air-yard role (363 air on 27 targets) overlaps Hawkins out and Tampa doubtful, plus BAL's softer middle (8.3 YPA). That pass overlap is partly cancelled by the 31% blitz that has already beaten this QB.

form: Avoid season averages. Henry last 4 rush yards 89, 73, 102, 58 (avg 80.5) vs a 83.5 line; weeks 4-6 were 64/233 (3.64 YPC, 77.7/game) — role stable, efficiency ordinary. Higgins last 4 rec yards 95, 90, 157, 22 (avg 91) vs 65.5, and he out-produced Chase in the weeks 3-5 sample. Flowers last 4 (84, 118, 53, 66) and Andrews last 4 (24, 27, 28, 4, all under 29.5) are Jackson-era and should not be ported. Brown's rush is unstable (last 4: 80, 61, 10, 39; weeks 3-5 only 36.7/game) into a 3.85 YPC BAL run defense. Meyers' weeks 3-5 line (16 targets / 123 yards) sits far above a 13.5 number but last 4 includes a 0. Perine is the change-of-pace (20 carries / 84 yards in weeks 3-5), not the lead back.

pro_edge.script_read: Spread is 3.0, inside the 3.5 underdog-throws-more flag, so do not auto-fade Henry for pass volume. Total 46.5 is moderate: some plays, not a shootout stack and not a weather slog. Blowout flag is off at 3 points, so starter snaps should mostly hold. The real lever is Jackson out, which points to Henry carries up and BAL pass efficiency down, while CIN still needs about 25 points.
pro_edge.best_price: No Pinnacle quote in the pack; anchor is consensus no-vig. Henry rushyds 83.5 over fair 0.502 / under 0.498, best over -114, best under -112.5. Higgins recyds 65.5 over fair 0.503, best over -114.5, best under -112. Neither price beats the anchor; the edge is matchup, not a stale number. Meyers over 13.5 at -120 is worse than fair 0.511. No two-sided price: Gesicki 22, Chase 82, Brown rush 41, Huntley rush 25, Perine rush 27.
pro_edge.lagging: No line-move log was precomputed, so no confirmed lagging flag. Spots that look off recent form and are not being bet: Bateman 19.5 vs weeks 4-6 36 yards/game; Andrews 29.5 vs 19.7 yards/game (may already be up for the QB change, or stale — cannot tell). Higgins 65.5 vs a 91-yard last-4 average looks un-juiced relative to form and to the secondary injuries.
pro_edge.sleepers: Jackson Out. No same-position QB with a pass prop on the board. Huntley rushyds 25 has no two-sided price, so replacement rush usage is not in a two-way market. Defensive outs/doubtful: Hawkins (S), Robinson (LB), Tampa (CB). Higgins 65.5 has not been pushed up toward his 90-yard form despite those DBs — sleeper-side note for the over. Flowers 64.5 is still a coin flip (no-vig 0.500) at his Jackson-era average, so that line did not come down for the QB change; that is a reason to avoid Flowers over, not to bet it.

pre_mortem: Monday, Henry under 83.5: Cincinnati, unafraid of Huntley, stacked the box, the 5.30 YPC figure had been built against real passing threats, and Henry's recent 3.64 YPC fell toward another 58-yard game while Hill or Huntley took the explosives. Higgins under 65.5: the 31% blitz did what Burrow's -0.11 EPA vs blitz said it would, quick throws went to Brown and Gesicki, Higgins repeated the 22-yard game, and Tampa played. Unknown wind is an unpriced killer for his air yards. Those counters are real, especially the box-stack, but they are not stronger than a leaky 5.30 YPC front for a 21-carry back at a coin-flip number, or a 25-yard cushion under Higgins' recent mean with two DBs out or doubtful.
slip_story: One competitive-game story, not a shootout and not a clock-kill blowout: Baltimore without Jackson runs through Henry, and Cincinnati still throws to its air-yards leader against a thinned secondary. The two legs win together if it stays within a score. Do not add Flowers over (needs Jackson-level passing), a total under (fights Higgins), or Brown rush over (BAL allows 3.85 YPC). No TD legs. Two legs only.
